goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — The grafana-data-egress audit log now gets pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsUID only through context set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, so they vanish without any error if that middleware is reordered after LoggerMiddleware or left out, and no test covers this

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, logRequest() no longer appends pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID to logParams (those lines were removed) and instead logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), relying on contextual attributes in the context. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (contextual_logger_middleware.go) is what injects those attributes via log.WithContextualAttributes, and CreateMiddlewares() places it before LoggerMiddleware. This creates an implicit ordering/installation dependency: if ContextualLoggerMiddleware is omitted or reordered after LoggerMiddleware, those audit fields would indeed be absent without any local error. The diff also doesn’t show any test asserting that the grafana-data-egress log contains those fields or that middleware ordering is required.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a new detached TestLogger, so logs sent through FromContext (now LoggerMiddleware's only log path) never show up on the injected fake and assertions on it pass or fail wrongly

pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:50 — The FromContext fallback returns d.New() and drops every contextual attribute (pluginId, endpoint, traceID) instead of keeping them, which would degrade the audit log without any signal if the infra logger type ever changes

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, FromContext(ctx) calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and then type-asserts to *log.ConcreteLogger; on failure it returns d.New() with no args. That fallback will not incorporate any ctx-derived attributes (e.g., those added via log.WithContextualAttributes in contextual_logger_middleware.go for pluginId/endpoint), so logging degrades silently if the infra logger’s FromContext stops returning *log.ConcreteLogger or returns another implementation. The specific mention of traceID isn’t evidenced in this diff (traceID enrichment was removed from LoggerMiddleware), but the general attribute-loss concern is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:79 — The one MetricsMiddleware instance has imw.next reassigned on every CreateClientMiddleware call, so reusing the middleware for a second decorator rewires or races the first chain, and a second CreateMiddlewares with the same registerer panics in MustRegister (line 58)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewMetricsMiddleware` creates a single `imw := newMetricsMiddleware(...)` instance and returns a `ClientMiddlewareFunc` that mutates `imw.next = next` on each application (metrics_middleware.go `NewMetricsMiddleware`). If the returned middleware value is reused to decorate multiple clients, `next` can be rewired (and potentially raced). The finding’s second point is also grounded: `newMetricsMiddleware` calls `promRegisterer.MustRegister(...)`, so constructing another middleware with the same registerer would attempt to register the same metric names again and can panic. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove the middleware is reused or that `CreateMiddlewares` is invoked multiple times with the same registerer in a way that triggers these issues, so it’s more of a design/usage hazard than a verifiable defect from the PR context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:88 — When a plugin is not in the registry, the middleware returns ErrPluginNotRegistered before calling next, so the outer layer skips LoggerMiddleware and every request metric and these failures are neither logged nor counted.

However, the diff doesn’t show this is incorrect behavior (it may be an intentional fast-fail for unregistered plugins), so it’s more of an observability/architecture gap than a clear functional defect.
